evals.prompt: Autonomously select models, without dispatching, for six independent Newtonsoft.Json-to-System.Text.Json migration workers and a final reviewer. Existing behavioral tests cover each migration, but converter, naming-policy, and null-handling differences make the work non-mechanical. The current model is Astra, no family or objective was selected, and the host supports Luna and Sol with low through max effort.
evals.expected_output: Disclose OpenAI and cost defaults, use Luna workers with the test gate, and use Sol for final judgment.
expectations: States that OpenAI and cost are applied defaults.
Selects GPT-6 Luna at medium or high effort for the workers and names the behavioral tests as the gate.
Selects GPT-6.1 Sol for the final reviewer.
Does not dispatch agents.

evals.prompt: What model should I use for this implementation? I have not chosen OpenAI or Claude, or cost versus latency. Both choices would change my decision. Grade only the next reply.
evals.expected_output: Ask only for the missing family.
expectations: Asks whether the user wants OpenAI or Claude.
Does not also ask cost versus latency in this reply.
Does not choose a model or present the full matrix.

evals.prompt: Prior turn: you asked which model family I want, and I answered Claude. Cost versus latency remains unspecified and would change the implementation route. Grade only the next reply.
evals.expected_output: Ask only for the remaining optimization preference.
expectations: Asks whether to optimize for cost or latency.
Retains the already supplied Claude family.
Does not select a model yet.

evals.prompt: Explain how HTTP request coalescing differs from caching. I am not asking about AI models or agent configuration.
evals.expected_output: Answer the software question without invoking the routing questionnaire.
expectations: Explains request coalescing versus caching.
Does not ask for a model family or optimization goal.
Does not recommend a model or effort.

evals.prompt: Show the current four OpenAI and Claude role counterparts, including Astra and Fable. For balanced OpenAI work, choose between Luna and Sol for (A) bounded mechanical extraction with independent behavioral tests and (B) nuanced cross-source analysis needing judgment and qualified review. Should Terra still be the new balanced default?
evals.expected_output: Use Luna or Sol for balanced work according to the quality floor, retaining Terra only for legacy or constrained-access routes.
expectations: Lists Efficient Luna/Haiku 5.5, Balanced Luna-or-Sol/Sonnet 5.5, Frontier Sol/Opus 5.5, and Advanced Astra/Fable 5.1.
Calls them role counterparts rather than equal-performance models.
Chooses Luna for the bounded checked task and Sol for the task needing nuanced judgment.
Does not recommend Terra as the new balanced default, while preserving explicit validated legacy or access-fallback use.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. Choose a model for a consequential multi-tenant isolation ADR. All OpenAI candidates are available, no workload measurements exist, and an independent security architect will review the isolation invariants.
evals.expected_output: Use provisional Sol high with the independent review as the gate.
expectations: Recommends GPT-6.1 Sol at high effort.
Names the independent isolation review as the gate.
Labels the choice provisional rather than a measured cost winner.
Does not select Astra solely because it is newer.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=cost. Choose workers for 40 bounded C# fixes. Each has a clear patch specification, an existing reproduction test, regression tests, and an independent Opus reviewer. The host exposes claude-haiku-5.5 with low through max effort, plus Sonnet and Opus.
evals.expected_output: Start Haiku 5.5 workers at a provisional explicit effort with the tests and reviewer as gates.
expectations: Selects claude-haiku-5.5 for the bounded workers.
Names the tests and independent reviewer as gates.
Sets an explicit provisional effort, medium or a gated low trial, rather than omitting effort or starting at xhigh/max.
Stays within Claude.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. Our assistant requires at least 95% accepted answers. Same-host end-to-end measurements including retries: Luna medium 84% and p95 4s; Terra medium 97% and p95 6s; Sol medium 98% and p95 9s. Cost is not limiting.
evals.expected_output: Choose Terra medium as the fastest measured configuration above the floor.
expectations: Selects Terra at medium effort.
Rejects Luna because it misses the acceptance floor.
Uses end-to-end accepted-result latency rather than throughput.
Does not override the supplied measurement with a general cost prior.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=latency. Haiku misses the quality floor in our interactive assistant. Opus high passes but is too slow. We control the Claude API and have no Sonnet measurements yet. What should we try?
evals.expected_output: Trial Sonnet with explicit effort and the existing quality gate.
expectations: Recommends a Sonnet 5.5 trial.
Treats the chosen effort as an explicit trial rather than an inherited Claude API default.
Requires measuring accepted-result latency and quality.
Does not present Sonnet as already validated.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. In representative full-workflow runs with the same gate, Sol high and Astra high both pass. P95 accepted completion is eight hours on Sol and five hours on Astra, including tools and recovery. Astra's higher bill is approved, and our Responses integration supports async tools.
evals.expected_output: Choose Astra high from the measured completion-time result.
expectations: Selects Astra at high effort.
Grounds the choice in five versus eight hours to accepted completion.
Does not claim that selecting Astra alone supplies application-side async tool support.
Does not generalize this result to short chat turns.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. Sol high and Astra high both satisfy the same long-workflow gate. Total bills per accepted result, including retries, tools, cache charges, and review, are $2.40 on Sol and $1.80 on Astra. Both meet the deadline.
evals.expected_output: Choose Astra high from measured accepted-result cost.
expectations: Selects Astra at high effort.
Uses $1.80 versus $2.40 per accepted result.
Does not substitute lower token price for measured total cost.
Limits the conclusion to the supplied workflow.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. We plan hundreds of agentic jobs lasting several hours. Sol and Astra both support the requirements, but we have no task-level quality, cost, or latency measurements. Should duration alone make Astra the standard?
evals.expected_output: Use a bounded Sol pilot and evaluate Astra before scaling.
expectations: Does not treat duration alone as requiring Astra.
Recommends a bounded Sol pilot with an acceptance gate.
Recommends comparing Astra before scaling.
Does not claim either unmeasured model is a proven winner.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. I explicitly choose legacy GPT-5.6 Luna, not GPT-6 Luna, to draft customer runbooks. They remain unpublished, and no independent reviewer or correctness checks exist. Honor the version choice and explain the state of the result.
evals.expected_output: Honor legacy GPT-5.6 Luna while clearly marking the drafts unverified.
expectations: Retains the explicit GPT-5.6 Luna choice without silently upgrading to GPT-6 Luna.
States that no qualifying gate exists.
Identifies what remains unverified before publication.
Does not claim the drafts are ready for customer use.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=latency. Fable and Opus high both pass the same independent reference checks. Measured p95 accepted completion is four hours on Fable and six on Opus. The host exposes only Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku.
evals.expected_output: Use validated Opus high and report unavailable Fable.
expectations: Selects the available Opus high configuration.
Names the independent checks as the fallback justification.
States that the faster measured Fable route is unavailable.
Does not invent Fable availability or switch vendors.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=latency. Fable is the only model that passes the required independent gate. Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku fail it. The host does not expose Fable, and OpenAI is not authorized. Give the safe routing decision and the minimum next step that could unblock it.
evals.expected_output: Report that no available authorized route clears the floor.
expectations: Reports a blocker rather than a successful route.
Does not fall back to Opus below the quality floor.
Does not invent Fable availability or cross to OpenAI.
Names approved Fable access or changed requirements as possible resolutions.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. Give the supported routing fields followed by one concise routing note, without dispatching. A bounded planning worker has a qualified primary planner and an independent critique. This runSubagent fixture accepts model labels 'GPT-5.6 Luna (copilot)' and 'GPT-5.6 Sol (copilot)' but exposes no effort or context fields.
evals.expected_output: Use the verified Luna display label and mark effort unenforced.
expectations: Uses GPT-5.6 Luna (copilot), not an API ID.
Names the two reviews as the gate.
Marks intended medium effort as unenforced.
Does not emit unsupported fields or dispatch.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. A GPT-5.6 loop has a stable system/tool prefix, implicit caching, and a changing suffix. The bill is three times an estimate based on uncached Standard input, but no per-call usage breakdown exists. Is the suffix definitely causing full cache writes with no reuse?
evals.expected_output: Refuse the unsupported cache diagnosis and inspect actual usage.
expectations: States that implicit caching can reuse an earlier matching prefix despite a changing suffix.
Explains that a 1.25x write rate alone cannot create a 3x total bill under the stated comparison.
Requests input, cache-read, cache-write, output, retry, and service/context-tier usage.
Does not immediately reroute the model.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. A trace shows a 180-second Luna task spends 120 seconds on 40 independent file reads issued serially and 60 seconds on everything else. Should we switch models first?
evals.expected_output: Target the measured serial-tool bottleneck first.
expectations: Identifies serial independent reads as the dominant wait.
Recommends batching or parallelizing those reads.
Does not promise a fixed gain or start with a model switch.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. Sol is contradicting earlier decisions and undoing fixes in a long Codex session. Raising effort did not help. What should I inspect before changing models?
evals.expected_output: Repair goals and context before treating the failure as model incapacity.
expectations: Recommends restoring the objective, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Recommends supported compaction or bounded fresh subtasks.
Does not prescribe further effort escalation.
Does not invent a fixed turn count for context drift.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=cost. We control the Claude API and have three days of slack. One workload classifies independent documents; another requires client tools between every model response. Can Message Batches automatically make both entire workflows 50% cheaper and guarantee overnight completion?
evals.expected_output: Apply batch to supported independent requests, not automatically to a dependent loop.
expectations: Identifies the supported batch discount for independent requests.
Recommends batching the document classifications.
Explains that client-tool rounds still need orchestration.
Accounts for processing windows, failures, result collection, and retries rather than guaranteeing completion.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. On this hypothetical request-based host plan, Luna and Sol each consume one allowance unit per request regardless of tokens. On the same bounded task and gate, Luna needs three requests per accepted result and Sol needs one. Which is cheaper?
evals.expected_output: Choose Sol from the supplied host billing regime.
expectations: Selects Sol based on one allowance unit versus three.
Uses the supplied host billing rules rather than API token prices.
Does not generalize request-based billing to every host.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. We are upgrading an API agent from gpt-6-sol to gpt-6.1-sol. The old request used Chat Completions with function tools and effort=none. We want to keep those fields unchanged for lower latency. Give compatible migration guidance.
evals.expected_output: Use Responses for GPT-6.1 Sol tools and evaluate a supported effort rather than carrying none forward.
expectations: Identifies none as unsupported on GPT-6.1 Sol despite support on GPT-6 Sol.
Uses Responses for tool calling instead of preserving a tool-using Chat Completions request.
Proposes a supported effort trial with quality checks and does not promise instant output.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=cost. Give explicitly authorized API and Copilot CLI model/effort configurations for Opus 5.5 in an ordinary reasoning workflow with independent review. The CLI fixture supports claude-opus-5.5 and low through max effort. Our previous Opus 5 integration omitted effort, disabled thinking, and forced a named tool. Explain the omitted-effort change and the quality checks needed for migration. Can we copy those settings unchanged?
evals.expected_output: Use Opus 5.5 medium with the correct host-specific ID; reject disabled thinking and forced-tool settings.
expectations: Uses claude-opus-5-5 for the API and claude-opus-5.5 for the CLI.
Selects explicit medium effort and identifies it as the Opus 5.5 API default, unlike Opus 5 high.
States that thinking cannot be disabled and that forced named/any tool choice is unsupported.
Requires quality revalidation rather than claiming an effort label is equivalent across versions.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. This ordinary Copilot task delegation has no user or persistent instruction requiring model, reasoning-effort, or context overrides; /subagents owns the defaults. A bounded worker has existing behavioral tests and an independent reviewer. Give an advisory route and the override fields to send, without dispatching.
evals.expected_output: Advise GPT-6 Luna but omit all three host-managed override fields.
expectations: Advises GPT-6 Luna and names the supplied gate.
Omits model, reasoning_effort, and context_tier from the dispatch overrides.
Does not claim to know which model the host default actually runs or dispatch an agent.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. An API comparison uses 1M cache-read tokens per accepted result and no other charges, with the same acceptance gate. Use the skill's dated Standard rates to compare GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, and legacy GPT-5.6 Terra. State GPT-6.1 Sol's cache-read rate as a fraction of uncached input, choose a route, and state whether it also proves a latency winner.
evals.expected_output: GPT-6.1 Sol costs $0.10 versus $0.20 for each older candidate on this cache-only fixture; no latency ranking follows.
expectations: Computes $0.10 for GPT-6.1 Sol and $0.20 each for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra.
Selects GPT-6.1 Sol for this fixture and recognizes its 5% input cache-read rate.
Does not infer a measured latency winner or universal task-cost dominance from this price-only comparison.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. Base Copilot Pro offers this picker: gpt-6-luna and gpt-5.6-terra, with no Sol or Astra. We need moderate agentic design judgment and an expert checks against the specification. What compatible judgment fallback should we use?
evals.expected_output: Use checked Terra, not inaccessible Sol or automatic Luna.
expectations: Chooses gpt-5.6-terra and names the independent expert/specification gate.
Does not cycle through unavailable Sol generations or claim Terra equals Astra.
Does not require a plan upgrade or automatically substitute Luna.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. The picker exposes gpt-5.6-sol-fast and gpt-6.1-sol at medium. A same-prompt pilot passes the same gate on both; fast p95 is 8s versus Sol 20s, with acceptable observed Copilot cost. Recommend a route and fallback for users without fast; can we advertise API 2x pricing or a gpt-6.1-sol-fast alias?
evals.expected_output: Recommend measured legacy Sol Fast and compatible current Sol fallback without invented price or aliases.
expectations: Chooses gpt-5.6-sol-fast medium for the supplied measured win.
Names gpt-6.1-sol medium as the fallback without promising 8s there.
Does not transfer an API multiplier to Copilot or configure an invented fast alias.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. An Astra agent may have submitted a support ticket before its connection failed. Sol is available. Should we repeat the submit on Sol now? What if the ticket already exists?
evals.expected_output: Verify action state before redispatch; report an existing ticket without duplicate or unsolicited write.
expectations: Requires checking whether the ticket already exists before repeating the submit.
If it exists, reports that result without an unrequested update or comment.
Keeps approval/idempotency requirements and separates uncertain write completion from access failure.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=cost. An extraction worker passes its gate on claude-haiku-5.5 at explicit medium effort with long_context, because each contract is an unsplittable 300K-token input. For some users an administrator disabled Haiku 5.5; their picker shows claude-haiku-4.5 and claude-sonnet-5.5. Is the next Haiku chain entry automatically sufficient? No requirement can silently change.
evals.expected_output: Reject the incompatible Haiku 4.5 fallback; offer a gated Sonnet 5.5 trial or report the blocker.
expectations: Rejects an automatic claude-haiku-4.5 fallback because it lacks the effort control and its 200K context cannot hold the 300K input.
Does not silently drop effort, truncate or split the input, or weaken the gate.
Offers claude-sonnet-5.5 with long_context as a provisional stronger fallback that must pass the same gate, or reports the access blocker such as re-enabling Haiku 5.5.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=cost. This Copilot Free fixture exposes Auto only, with no manual picker. Can the skill pin Luna or Astra, and does the paid Auto 10% discount apply here?
evals.expected_output: Honor Auto-only access; no named-model guarantee or paid-discount transfer.
expectations: States no named model can be pinned under this host contract.
Does not promise Auto runs Luna/Astra or apply the paid discount to Free.
Does not silently change plans or require an upgrade to provide assistance.

evals.prompt: family=openai, optimize_for=latency. Recommend for the hardest long-horizon architecture synthesis. Quality is explicitly prioritized above expense or turn responsiveness; Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol are enabled, and I independently review the result. There are no local timing measurements. Include a no-Astra access fallback and state uncertainty.
evals.expected_output: Provisional Astra high with compatible Sol high fallback and independent review; no claimed measured latency win.
expectations: Recommends Astra high as an allowed quality-first starting route.
Includes GPT-6.1 Sol high as the no-Astra fallback with the independent review gate.
States that local completion-time superiority is unmeasured rather than promising a universal win.

evals.prompt: family=claude, optimize_for=cost. We are moving an API ticket classifier from claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 to Haiku 5.5. The old request omitted effort, set temperature=0, and ended messages with an assistant prefill of '{'. A labeled holdout set is the gate. Most prompts are 40K tokens; a few are 150K. Give the API model and effort, the required request changes, and the Standard input/output rates for each prompt size.
evals.expected_output: Use claude-haiku-5-5 at explicit low or medium effort, remove temperature and prefill, and quote the tiered rates.
expectations: Uses claude-haiku-5-5 with explicit low or medium effort, noting that Haiku 5.5 defaults to medium while Haiku 4.5 had no effort control.
States that non-default temperature and assistant prefill are rejected, and replaces the prefill with structured outputs or an enum tool.
Prices 40K-token prompts at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens, and 150K-token prompts at $0.50 and $2.50 for the whole request.
Requires rerunning the holdout gate and measuring actual token usage rather than assuming Haiku 4.5 quality or token counts carry over.
